title: Hand of Straights
keyIdea: The smallest card left must be the lowest card of its group, so the group is forced: first, first + 1, …, first + groupSize − 1. Repeatedly take that run from a sorted count map; if a card is missing, it's impossible.

approaches.name: Greedy with an ordered map
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). Size check; map<int,int> counts; while not empty: first = smallest key; remove one of first..first + k − 1, failing if any is missing.
approaches.why: Each card is decremented once, each map operation O(log n).

quiz.q: Why must the smallest card start a group?
options: No smaller card is left to come before it in a run
hand.size() % groupSize == 0, or it can't split evenly
